name: cellulose
gene_ids: gh94, gh1, gh2, gh3, gh5, gh9, gh16, gh116, gh6, gh8, gh10, gh124, gh12, gh44, gh45, gh7, gh48, aa10, aa15, aa16, aa9, aa11, aa13
rule: [gh5 | gh8 | gh9 | gh10 | gh12 | gh44 | gh45 | gh124] & [gh6 | gh7 | gh48] & [gh1 | gh3 | gh94 | gh116]
notes: a genome is capable of cellulose degradation if it encodes at least one endo-acting cellulase, one exo-acting cellobiohydrolase, and one β-glucosidase. lpmos (aa9, aa10, aa16) provide an oxidative bonus that enhances but is not essential for cellulose degradation.

name: hemicellulose
gene_ids: gh113, gh134, gh26, gh5, gh130, ce2, ce17, gh2, gh99, gh76, gh92, gh38, gh63, gh47, gh125, gh9, gh12, gh16, gh44, gh45, gh48, gh74, aa9, gh31, gh43, gh10, gh11, gh51, ce1, ce4
notes: for a genome to have hemicellulose degradation capability, it should encode: at least one backbone hydrolase, one side-chain/esterase, and optionally an lpmo for enhanced activity.

name: lignin
gene_ids: aa1, mco, aa2, dyp, aa3_2, aa5_1, aa8, aa3_1
rule: [aa1 | mco | aa2 | dyp] & [aa3_1 | aa3_2 | aa5_1 | aa8]
notes: for a genome to have lignin degradation capability, it should encode: at least one oxidative polymer attack enzyme (aa1, mco, aa2, dyp) and one redox support enzyme (aa3_1, aa3_2, aa5_1, aa8) to drive oxidative depolymerization.

name: pectin
gene_ids: gh28, pl1, pl2, pl3, pl4, pl9, pl10, pl11, pl22, pl26, gh78, gh106, gh138, gh139, gh143, ce8, gh105, gh4, ce12, gh2
notes: for a genome to have pectin degradation capability, it should encode: at least one backbone-cleaving hydrolase or lyase, one debranching or accessory enzyme, and one esterase for de-methylation or de-acetylation.

name: starch
notes: for a genome to have starch degradation capability, it should encode: at least one amylolytic hydrolase (gh13, gh14, gh15, gh57, gh97, gh119, gh126, gh133) and optionally an lpmo (aa13) for oxidative enhancement.

name: anaerobic aromatic hydrocarbon degradation
notes: for a genome to have anaerobic aromatic hydrocarbon degradation capability, it should encode at least one anaerobic aromatic activation enzyme: benzylsuccinate synthase (bssabc, k07540) for toluene via fumarate addition, or  benzoyl-coa reductase (bama, k04114) for benzoyl-coa reductive dearomatization. presence of both indicates likely capacity for anaerobic degradation of aromatic hydrocarbons in marine sediments.

name: acetate (scfa)
notes: acetate production can occur via the phosphate acetyltransferase–acetate kinase route (k00625 and k00925, both required) or alternative ligase (k01905) or hydrolase (k01067) pathways. either route yields acetate from acetyl-coa.

name: butyrate (scfa)
notes: butyrate formation proceeds via phosphate butyryltransferase (k00634) coupled with either butyrate kinase (k00929) or medium-chain acyl-coa synthetase (k01896). both steps are required for full conversion.

name: lactate (scfa)
notes: lactate formation can occur through l-lactate dehydrogenases (k00016, k00101) or d-lactate variants (k03778, k03777). presence of any indicates capacity for pyruvate reduction to lactate.

name: propionate (scfa)
notes: propionate formation requires both propionate kinase (k19697) and propionate coa-transferase (k01026) for coa-dependent conversion of intermediates to propionate.

name: pyruvate (scfa)
notes: pyruvate conversion to acetyl-coa occurs via one of three enzyme complexes: pyruvate dehydrogenase (k00163), 2-oxoacid ferredoxin oxidoreductase (k00174), or formate-acetyltransferase (k00656). presence of any indicates potential for acetyl-coa formation.

name: alcohol
notes: for a genome to have alcohol conversion capability, it should encode: at least one alcohol dehydrogenase or related enzyme involved in ethanol and higher-alcohol interconversion.

name: fatty acid degradation β-oxidation
notes: for a genome to have fatty acid degradation capability via β-oxidation, it should encode at least one acyl-coa dehydrogenase (fade,k06445,k00249,k00255,k09479), one enoyl-coa hydratase (fadb,k13767,k01825), and thiolase (fada,k00632) completing one full β-oxidation cycle.

name: aerobic ch4 oxidation
notes: for a genome to have ch₄ oxidation capability, it must encode at least one methane monooxygenase complex (pmmo or smmo), which catalyzes the conversion of methane to methanol.

name: alkane tranformation (archaeal)
notes: for a genome to have anaerobic alkane transformation capability, it should encode for a methyl-com reductase catalytic subunit (mcra, k00399). encoding for other subunits (mcrabcdg, k00399,k00401,k00402,k00421,k00422) is detected. this annotation will identify canonical mcr and divergent mcr or mcr-like sequences mapping to the same ko, performing an mcra phylogeny is recommended. presence of an mcr without phylogenetic placement can suggest multiple different metabolisms falling under anaerobic alkane transformation capability (various forms of methanogenesis, reverse methanogenesis, anaerobic alkane degradation).

name: co2 fixation
notes: for a genome to have co₂ fixation capability via the acetyl-coa pathway, it should encode: the complete codh/acs complex (cdha, cdhb, cdhc, cdhd, and cdhe subunits), which together catalyze co₂ reduction to acetyl-coa. this is distinct from the wood-ljungdahl pathway row which additionally requires (eastern) methyl branch genes.

name: wood-ljungdahl pathway
notes: for a genome to have wood-ljungdahl co2 fixation capability, it should encode the complete western brnach codh/acs complex for either the bacterial (k00198, k14138) or archaeal (k00192, k00195, k00193, k00194, k00197) and have at least one eastern/methyl branch entry point (fdha k01938 or fhs k05299). presence of both branches indicates full reductive acetyl-coa synthesis from co2 molecules.

name: 3-hydroxypropionate/4-hydroxybutyrate (3hp/4hb) cycle
notes: for a genome to have 3hp/4hb co₂ fixation capability, it should encode all of the 3 following genes - 1) k14534, 2) either malonyl-coa reductase or acetyl-coa carboxylase (k15017, or k18603-5, respectively) 3) either k15039 and k18602) .presence of all three modules indicates complete autotrophic co₂ fixation via the 3hp/4hb cycle, something previously characteristic of crenarchaeota in marine sediments.

name: calvin-benson-bassham (cbb) cycle
notes: for a genome to have cbb cycle co₂ fixation capability it should encode ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase large chain (rbcl, k01601), phosphoribulokinase (prk, k00855), and one ribulose-phosphate 3-epimerase (rpe, k01783) to differentiate the cbb cycle from the rhp metabolic pathway.

name: reductive glycine pathway
notes: for a genome to have reductive glycine pathway co₂ fixation capabilit, it should encode at least 3 proteins/subunuts of the glycine cleavage system (k00283, k00282, k02437, and k00605) and at least 5 of the glycine reductase  (k10671, k10672, k00384, k21577, k21576, k03671, and k10670).

name: rtca cycle
notes: for a genome to have reductive tca cycle it should encode either 1 atp-citrate lyase (k15233 or k15232) or citryl-coa synthetase+citryl-coa lyase (k15233 or k15232, and k15234).

name: rump pathway (non-methanogenic methylotrophy type i)
notes: for a genome to have rump pathway methylotrophy capability it should encode hps (k08093,k13831,k13812) and phi (k08094) a methanol dehydrogenase (mdh, k00093,k23995,k17066,k14028,k14029) and at least one  together these suggest capacity to convert methanol and formaledehyde into usable fructose 6-phosphate.

name: serine pathway (non-methanogenic methylotrophy type ii)
notes: for a genome to have serine pathway methylotrophy capability it should encode serine-glyoxylate transaminase (sgt, k00830), hydroxypyruvate reductase (hpr, k00018), and malyl-coa lyase (mcl, k08691). additional encoding of serine hydroxymethyltransferase (shmt, k00600) further supports likelihood of having this pathway.

name: hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis
notes: for a genome to have hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis capability it should encode the mcr complex (mcrabg, k00399+k00401+k00402), the mtr complex core subunits (mtra-e+h, k00577-k00581+k00584; mtrf/g omitted due to less consistent annotations), at least 2 of the 4 upper c1 pathway steps (ftr-k00672, mch-k01499, mtd-k00319 or hmd-k13942, mer-k00320), and at least one fwd/fmd subunit (k00200-k00205). this combination distinguishes hydrogenotrophic methanogens from obligate methylotrophic lineages (which lack mtr) and from aceticlastic methanogens (which lack the upper c1 pathway). anme archaea encode the same genes in reverse so performing an mcra phylogeny is highly recommended to confirm methanogenesis direction. methylotrophs that also do hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis e.g. canonical methanosarcinales) will present as matched to this row and "methylotrophic and aceticlastic methanogenesis". distinguishing between methanogenesis pathways via gene presence/absence is not recommended for genomes less than 90% complete.

name: methylotrophic and aceticlastic methanogenesis
notes: for a genome to have methylotrophic or aceticlastic methanogenesis capability it should encode the mcr complex (mcrabg, k00399+k00401+k00402) plus at least one substrate-specific entry point. i.e. methanol, methylamines, methylated sulfur, or acetate . for methanol potential enzymes are mtab (k04480), mtaa (k14080), or mtac (k14081); for methylamines potential enzymes are mtba (k14082), mtmb/monomethylamine methyltransferase (k16176), mtmc/monomethylamine corrinoid protein (k16177), mtbb/dimethylamine methyltransferase (k16178), mtbc/dimethylamine corrinoid protein (k16179), mttb/trimethylamine methyltransferase (k14083), or mttc/trimethylamine corrinoid protein (k14084); for methylated sulfur potential enzymes are mtsa (k16954) or mtsb (k16955); for acetate, enzymes are acka+pta (k00925+k00625) or acs (k01895), combined with codh/acs core subunits cdhc+cdhe+cdhd (k00193+k00197+k00194). here, aceticlastic methanogenesis overlaps with co2 fixation and wood-ljungdahl rows, but is distinguished with the presence of the mcr complex. performing an mcra phylogeny is recommended to distinguish between methanogenesis and anaerobic methanotrophy. distinguishing between methanogenesis pathways via gene presence/absence is not recommended for genomes less than 90% complete.

name: n2o to n2
notes: the reduction of nitrous oxide (n₂o) to dinitrogen gas (n₂) is catalyzed by nitrous oxide reductase (nosz, k00376). presence of this gene indicates the potential for the final step of denitrification, converting n₂o into n₂.

name: no3 to no2
notes: nitrate reduction to nitrite can occur through either the membrane-bound nar system (k00370 and k00371, both required) or the periplasmic nap system (k02567 and k02568, both required). either system completes the nitrate transformation step.

name: dnra, no3 to nh4
notes: dnra reduces nitrate to ammonium through a two-step process: nitrate reduction via nar or nap systems, followed by nitrite reduction via nrf or nir enzymes. presence of one nitrate reductase system and one nitrite reductase system indicates dnra capability.

name: no2 to no
notes: nitrite reduction to nitric oxide (no) is carried out by either nirs (k00368) or nirk (k15864). presence of either gene indicates capacity for nitrate/nitrite reduction in denitrification.

name: no to n2o
notes: the conversion of nitric oxide (no) to nitrous oxide (n₂o) is catalyzed by nitric oxide reductase, encoded by norb (k04561) in bacteria or cyp55 (k15877) in fungi. presence of either gene indicates the capacity to perform this denitrification step

name: assimilatory nitrate reduction
notes: assimilatory nitrate reduction = nitrate → nitrite via narb or nr or nasab, and nitrite → ammonium via ferredoxin nira, nad(p)h forms, or the k26138/k26139 pair. presence of one option from each step indicates pathway capability.

name: no2 to no3
notes: aerobic nitrate oxidation (nitrite oxidation) is the second step of nitrification, where nitrite is oxidized to nitrate by the nxr complex (nxrab) under oxic conditions, completing the conversion of reduced nitrogen to its most oxidized form.

name: aerobic ammonium oxidation
notes: aerobic ammonium oxidation converts ammonia to nitrite through sequential reactions catalyzed by ammonia monooxygenase and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase. presence of one ammonia monooxygenase subunit set and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase indicates this capability.

name: anaerobic ammonium
notes: anammox requires nitrite → no (nirk or nirs), hydrazine synthesis via hzs (hzsa/b/c), and hydrazine oxidation to n₂ by hdh.

name: n2 fixation
notes: nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric n₂ to ammonium through the nitrogenase enzyme complex. functional capacity is indicated by the presence of all subunits for either the mo-nitrogenase (nif) or the v-nitrogenase (vnf) system, as either complete complex can catalyze n₂ reduction.

name: assimilation
notes: presence of ammonium assimilation genes indicates microbial potential to incorporate inorganic ammonium (nh₄⁺) into organic nitrogen compounds such as glutamate, glutamine, and asparagine. this process reflects nitrogen retention within biomass rather than oxidative or mineralization pathways, contributing to overall ecosystem nitrogen conservation.

name: ammonium transformation
notes: ammonium oxidation (nh₃ to no₂⁻) requires both ammonia monooxygenase (any of k28504, k10944, k10945, or k10946) and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase (k10535). presence of both indicates this process. note: k10944/k10945/k10946 are shared with the aerobic ch4 oxidation row and the presence of k10535 is the distinguishing marker confirming ammonium oxidation.

name: nitrate transformation
notes: nitrate transformation represents the combined capacity for nitrate (no₃⁻) reduction to nitrite (no₂⁻) and subsequent nitrite reduction to nitric oxide (no). it integrates both the nar/nap (nitrate reductase) and nir (nitrite reductase) steps, capturing the overall microbial potential to transform nitrate into reduced nitrogen intermediates.

name: urea transformation
notes: urea hydrolysis requires the full urease enzyme complex, composed of subunits urea (k01430), ureb (k01429), and urec (k01428). all three genes are needed to complete urea transformation to ammonium and co₂.

name: assimilatory sulfate reduction to sulfide
notes: for a genome to have assimilatory sulfate reduction metabolism it should encode a sulfate adenylyltransferase (sat-k00958, or cysnd-(k00955+k00957 or k00956+k00957)), apr reductase (k05907) or cysc+cysh (k00955 or k00860 + k00390), and cysi, cysj, or sir for final reduction of sulfite to sulfide (k00381,k00380, or k00392). presence of these genes indicates capacity to assimilate inorganic sulfate into organic biomass.

name: dissimilatory oxi/red sulfate to sulfite
notes: for a genome to have dissimilatory reduction or oxidation capability between sulfate and sulfite it should encode sulfate adenylyltransferase (sat, k00958) and adenylylsulfate reductase (aprab, k00394+k00395) for redox transitions between sulfite and sulfide.

name: dissimilatory oxi/red sulfite to sulfide
notes: for a genome to have dissimilatory reduction or oxidation capability between sulfite and sulfide it should encode dissimilatory sulfite reductase subunits (dsra and dsrb, k11180 and k11181) or the asrc sulfite reductase (k00385). presence of asrc rather than dsrab suggests anaerobic sulfite reduction without possibility for oxidative capacity. with the presence of dsrab it's recommended to investigate the dsrab operon and phylogenies of the dsra and dsrb placement is recommended for confirmation of reduction/oxidation capacity.

name: elemental sulfur reduction
notes: for a genome to have elemental sulfur reduction capability, it should encode: the sulfur reductase complex (srea-k17219, sreb-k17220, srec-k17221). presence indicates capacity to use elemental sulfur (s⁰) as a terminal electron acceptor under anaerobic conditions.

name: thiosulfate reduction
notes: for a genome to have thiosulfate reduction capability it should encode phsa-k08352 (extra confirmation comes from presence of phsb+c,k08353+k08354) alongside catalytic subunits dsrab (k11180 and k11181) or asrc (k00385) for final reduction to sulfide. the homology of phsabc genes should be investigated to determine substrate (i.e. thiosulfate vs polysulfide) specificity, distinguishing between phsabc and psrabc.

name: dms/dmsp cycling
notes: for a genome to have organosulfur cycling capacity it should encode ≥1 enzyme for transforimg at least one of the following substrates: dmsp,dms,dmso,methanethiol,dmsop,mmpa . key enzymes and their substrates include: dmsp lyases (dddd-k28073, dddl-k16953, dddp-k28067, dddw-k28068, dddy-k28069, dddx-k28072) producing dms from dmsp. dmsp demethylase (dmda-k17486) producing mmpa from dmsp. mmpa demethylation enzymes,dmdbcd (k20034+k20035+k20036), producing methanethiol from mmpa. dms monooxygenase (dmoa-k16967) producing methanethiol from dms. dms dehydrogenase (ddha-k16964) or trimethylamine monooxygenase (tmm-k18277) oxidizing dms to dmso. dmso reductase complex, dmsabc (k07306 +k07307 or k00184 +k07308 or k00185), or trimethylamine n-oxide reductase (tora-k07811) reducing dmso back to dms.

name: arsenic
notes: presence of arsenic resistance, oxidation, reduction, methylation, and efflux genes (ars, aio) indicates microbial potential for arsenic detoxification and transformation. includes oxidation (aioa/b), reduction (arsc), methylation (arsm), efflux (arsa/b/d), and regulation (arsr, aior/s).

name: cadmium
notes: presence of cadmium-associated resistance, regulation, and efflux genes indicates microbial potential for detoxification of cd²⁺ via efflux pumps (czc, czn, zitb, znta), transcriptional control (cadx, cmtr, czra, cusr/s), and sequestration or transport (cadd, dmef, cnr system), contributing to cadmium tolerance.

name: cobalt
notes: presence of cobalt resistance and transport genes indicates microbial capacity for co²⁺ detoxification, efflux, and regulation. includes transcriptional regulators (ncr, cnr, rcn), efflux systems (czc, dme, zitb, znta), transporters (cora/b/c, ctpd), and multi-component resistance operons (cme, cus, dmerf), enabling microbial adaptation to cobalt-rich or contaminated environments.

name: magnesium
notes: presence of magnesium homeostasis and transport genes indicates microbial capacity for mg²⁺ uptake, export, and regulation. includes primary transporters (cora, mgta, corb/c), p-type atpases for active transport, and regulatory proteins involved in maintaining cytoplasmic mg²⁺ balance under metal or osmotic stress conditions.

name: manganese
notes: presence of manganese transport and regulatory genes indicates microbial capacity for mn²⁺ uptake, efflux, and homeostasis. includes import systems (mnth, mnta, yfeabcd), p-type atpases (ctpc), efflux channels (mntp), and regulatory proteins (mntr) that maintain intracellular mn²⁺ balance, protect against oxidative stress, and support metalloenzyme function.

name: mercury
notes: presence of mercury resistance (mer) operon genes indicates microbial capacity for detoxification of inorganic and organic mercury compounds. includes transport and binding proteins (merc, mere, merf, merp, mert), regulatory components (merr, merd), and enzymes mediating reduction (mera) and cleavage of organomercurials (merb), collectively conferring hg²⁺ and methylmercury resistance.

name: nickel
notes: presence of nickel transport, efflux, and regulatory genes indicates microbial capacity for ni²⁺ acquisition, homeostasis, and detoxification. includes uptake systems (nikabcde, nixa, hupe), efflux pumps (czc, dme, cnr, nrs, rcn), cation diffusion facilitators (cnrt), and transcriptional regulators (ncr, nrs, nikr, rcnr) that maintain intracellular ni²⁺ balance and support ni-dependent metalloenzyme function under metal stress.

name: silver
notes: presence of silver resistance and efflux genes indicates microbial capacity for ag⁺ detoxification and homeostasis. includes multi-component efflux systems (sil, cus, cop), periplasmic chaperones (silf, sile, cusf), p-type atpases (silp, copa, copb), and two-component regulatory systems (cusrs) that coordinate ag⁺ sensing, transport, and reduction to mitigate toxicity in contaminated environments.

name: zinc
notes: presence of zinc resistance and homeostasis genes indicates microbial capacity for zn²⁺ uptake, sequestration, and efflux. includes import systems (znuabc, zipb, trob), regulators (zur, zrar/s, zntr, cadc/x), efflux transporters (czcabc, zitb, znta), metallothioneins and chaperones (smta, zint, zeva), and multidrug efflux systems (mdtabc) that together maintain intracellular zn²⁺ balance and mitigate metal stress.

name: copper
notes: presence of copper resistance, homeostasis, and transport genes indicates microbial potential for cu⁺/cu²⁺ detoxification, efflux, and redox regulation. this includes p-type atpases (copa, copb, ctpg, ctpv), multicopper oxidases (cueo, mco, cuto), periplasmic binding/chaperone systems (copc/d/z, pcoe, copl, cuer), regulatory systems (cusrs, cuer, corr, copy-tcry), and rnd/multidrug efflux complexes (cuscba, cmeabc, acrd, mctb), together facilitating copper detoxification and maintaining metal homeostasis under oxidative stress.

name: iron
notes: presence of iron storage, uptake, and efflux genes indicates microbial capacity for fe²⁺/fe³⁺ homeostasis and oxidative stress mitigation. this includes ferritin-like storage proteins (bfra, pfr, dpr-dps), fe(ii)/fe(iii) transport and reduction systems (fbpabc, yfeabcd, fpta, yqjh, efeo), efflux pumps (fief), and regulatory elements (pmra/b/c, ider). collectively these confer resistance to iron overload, oxidative damage, and contribute to redox balancing.

name: biofilms
notes: presence of alginate, psl, or pga/ica matrix biosynthesis genes indicates microbial capacity for biofilm formation, enhancing surface adhesion and persistence in marine environments. biofilm production supports microbial community stability, particle colonization, and resistance to physical disturbance in dynamic marine systems.

name: oxidative stress
notes: presence of oxidative stress defense genes (catalases, superoxide dismutases, glutathione biosynthesis enzymes, peroxidases, or laccases) indicates microbial potential to detoxify reactive oxygen species. this is relevant in marine microbes exposed to reactive oxygen species generated by chemical or biological oxidation systems and at oxic-anoxic interfaces.

name: flagella
notes: for a genome to have bacterial flagella motility, it should encode flagellin (flic, k02406), hook protein (flge, k02390), m-ring membrane anchor (flif, k02409), one p-ring proteins (flgi, k02394 and flga, k02386), l-ring precursor (flgh, k02393), and at least one motor stator protein (mota-k02556, motb-k02557, motc-k10564, motd-k10564 , motx-k21217, or moty-k21218), at least one switch protein (flig-k02410 or flim-k02416).

name: reductive dehalogenation
notes: presence of reductive dehalogenases: cpra-k21566 and/or pcea-k21647
